verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents creating machines through the API or CLI and managing resources programmatically through a REST API and the pspace CLI, authenticated with team-scoped API keys, so the provisioning core is first-party. The rest of the lifecycle is thin: there is no evidence of programmatic monitoring or explicit API/CLI teardown, auto-shutdown only stops idle machines, high-end GPUs such as H100 need approval, and no OpenAPI spec was found. Missing for 10: documented API/CLI monitoring of GPU machine status/metrics, explicit programmatic delete/destroy, an end-to-end agent-run workload example, an MCP server, a machine-readable API spec, and hands-on corroboration of headless operation.

support.subject: As an AI agent, I can provision a GPU, monitor it, run a workload, and tear it down end to end through documented APIs, CLI, or MCP without a human in the console

citations.quote: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
Programmatically manage Paperspace resources using conventional HTTP requests.
Programmatically manage resources using the Paperspace Command Line Interface.
API keys let you interact with Paperspace through the Core RESTful API, the Core JavaScript SDK, and Gradient command-line utility (CLI).
